summary: Exhaustive multi-dimension audit of the Multi-Agent Town Story Simulator with adversarial verification, plus academic-framing research
logs: Fanning out 5 dimension auditors + 1 research agent
Auditors returned 72 findings; merging with 28 lead findings

findings.title: Catch-all `except Exception: break` in the tick loop permanently kills the simulation on the first error
findings.description: run_simulation()'s while-loop wraps manager.tick() in `except Exception as e: print(...); break` (command.py:66-78), then falls through to sio.disconnect() and process exit. Exposure is guaranteed: every sim day at 03:00 tick() makes 7 synchronous LLM calls (manager.py:356-366), and generate_narrative calls response.raise_for_status() and re-raises on ANY non-2xx response (429 rate limit, 5xx, auth blip) plus any requests.ConnectionError (llm_handler.py:33-39); a KeyError on a response body lacking 'choices' rides the same path. One sim day is ~4.8 real minutes (0.4s/tick, +2 sim-minutes/tick), so the 7-call burst fires roughly every 5 minutes of wall time, making a crash near-inevitable in any long run. A single transient API hiccup terminates the whole process, losing all in-memory state (world clock, agent needs/money/relationships, memory streams, daily_stories) — and the failure is not resumable: a restart begins again at Monday day 1. The startup check_llm_api() (command.py:52) does not protect against mid-run failures.
findings.fix: In the loop, catch exceptions, log with traceback, and continue (optionally with a pause or crash counter) instead of break. Additionally wrap the 03:00 narrative block in manager.tick() in its own per-agent try/except so a failed diary/story is skipped or retried without aborting the tick, and isolate LLM calls behind retries so they never propagate into the tick loop.

verdict.justification: The claim is accurate at every verified point. (1) command.py:66-79: the tick loop wraps manager.tick() in `except Exception as e: print(...); break` (lines 76-78), falls through to sio.disconnect() (line 79), and the process exits — any single exception permanently ends the simulation. (2) manager.py:356-366: inside tick(), at hour==3/minute==0 (fires exactly once per sim day, since time starts at (8,0) and advances +2 even minutes per tick, manager.py:168), it makes unguarded calls to write_agent_diary for each agent plus compile_daily_story — simulation/config.py:302-337 defines exactly 6 agents, so 7 synchronous LLM calls per sim day, as claimed. (3) narrative_system.py:37,66 call generate_narrative with no try/except; llm_handler.py:33-39 uses requests.post with no timeout or retry, re-raises HTTPError on any non-2xx (429/5xx/auth) after printing, lets requests.ConnectionError propagate, and line 39 (`response.json()['choices'][0]...`) raises KeyError on a malformed body — all propagate through tick() into the loop's catch-all break. (4) Timing checks out: 720 ticks/day × 0.4s sleep (command.py:64,72) ≈ 4.8 real minutes per sim day, so the 7-call burst recurs roughly every 5 minutes of wall time with zero fault tolerance. (5) State loss/non-resumability confirmed: AgentManager.__init__ (manager.py:46-60) hard-codes time (8,0) and day_index 0 (Monday) and rebuilds agents from config; no persistence or reload mechanism exists anywhere, and check_llm_api (command.py:52) only runs at startup. Only trivial nitpicks: diary/story text files do persist on disk (narrative_system.py:41-42,68-69), though nothing reloads them so they are functionally lost to the running app; and ~4.8 min/day slightly understates wall time because the 7 blocking LLM calls add real seconds. Neither alters the mechanism or the Critical severity: one transient API hiccup in a mandatory per-day code path terminates the entire long-running simulation and destroys all simulation state.

findings.title: LLM requests have no timeout, no retry, and no rate-limit handling — a stalled connection freezes the simulation forever
findings.description: generate_narrative (llm_handler.py:33) and get_embedding (llm_handler.py:51) call requests.post without a timeout parameter, so requests waits indefinitely; the author knew about timeouts — check_llm_api passes timeout=10 (llm_handler.py:72) — but the two methods actually used during the run omit it. These calls execute inside manager.tick() on the single thread that drives the whole simulation, so a hung TCP connection or a server that accepts but never responds blocks the tick loop permanently: no exception, no state updates, sim clock stopped, process alive but dead, frontend frozen with no indication. There is also no retry/backoff and no 429 handling despite firing 6 back-to-back max_tokens=2048 requests every sim night, and no caching.
findings.fix: Pass an explicit timeout to every requests.post, e.g. timeout=(10, 120) (connect, read) for generate_narrative given the 2048-token generations and timeout=(10, 30) for get_embedding. Add tenacity-style exponential backoff honoring the Retry-After header for 429/5xx (e.g. 3 attempts), handle requests.exceptions.Timeout, and return structured errors instead of raising into the tick loop.

verdict.justification: Confirmed by direct code trace. simulation/llm_handler.py:33 (generate_narrative) and :51 (get_embedding) call requests.post with no timeout parameter, while check_llm_api at :72 passes timeout=10 — exactly as claimed; with no timeout, requests blocks indefinitely on a stalled read. The live execution path is proven: simulation/manager.py:356-366 runs inside tick() at sim-time 3:00 AM, synchronously calling narrative_system.write_agent_diary for every agent and then compile_daily_story, both of which invoke generate_narrative(prompt, max_tokens=2048) (simulation/narrative/narrative_system.py:37 and :66). tick() is driven by the single-threaded while-True loop in command.py:66-72, and the frontend receives state only via sio.emit('simulation_state_update', ...) inside that same loop — so one hung HTTP read permanently freezes the sim clock, all agent updates, and the UI, with the process still alive and no error surfaced. The no-retry/no-429-handling claim is also confirmed and is actually worse than described: raise_for_status (llm_handler.py:35-38) re-raises HTTPError, which propagates into command.py:76-78 ('except Exception ... break'), so a single transient 429/5xx permanently terminates the simulation loop. No caching exists anywhere. Two immaterial inaccuracies, neither of which overstates the defect: (1) get_embedding is currently dead code — no runtime caller exists anywhere in the repo (the project's own docs at docs/v2_upgrade/drafts/report_draft_sections.md:67 call it 'the currently-dead get_embedding path'), so the phrase 'the two methods actually used during the run' is wrong about get_embedding; the freeze mechanism rests entirely on generate_narrative, which is accurately described. (2) The nightly burst is 7 back-to-back max_tokens=2048 requests, not 6 (AGENT_CONFIG in simulation/config.py:300-337 defines 6 agents → 6 diaries + 1 town story), an undercount. Critical severity stands: one stalled connection bricks the entire simulation silently, and one transient HTTP error kills it outright.
verdict.corrected_description: generate_narrative (llm_handler.py:33) calls requests.post without a timeout parameter, so requests waits indefinitely; the author knew about timeouts — check_llm_api passes timeout=10 (llm_handler.py:72) — but the method actually exercised during the run omits it (get_embedding at llm_handler.py:51 also omits it, though it is currently dead code with no runtime caller). These calls execute inside manager.tick() (manager.py:356-366) on the single thread that drives the whole simulation (command.py:66-72), so a hung TCP connection or a server that accepts but never responds blocks the tick loop permanently: no exception, no state updates, sim clock stopped, process alive but dead, frontend frozen with no indication. There is also no retry/backoff and no 429 handling despite firing 7 back-to-back max_tokens=2048 requests every sim night (6 agent diaries + 1 town story), and no caching; worse, any HTTPError raised by raise_for_status propagates to command.py:76-78, whose 'except Exception: break' permanently terminates the simulation loop on a single transient 429/5xx.

findings.title: Seven synchronous LLM calls at 03:00 stall the tick loop for minutes every simulated day
findings.description: At hour==3, minute==0 (manager.py:356-366) tick() sequentially generates 6 agent diaries (write_agent_diary, max_tokens=2048, prompt explicitly asks for entries 'as complete and long as possible') plus 1 town story (max_tokens=2048), all as blocking non-streaming REST calls on the tick thread. At typical throughput each ~2048-token completion takes roughly 20-45s, so the nightly block stalls the loop ~2-5 minutes — roughly doubling the length of every ~4.8-minute sim day. During the stall no 'simulation_state_update' is emitted, agents freeze, simulated time stops, the frontend appears frozen at 03:00, and pause/resume handler effects cannot be observed because the loop shares its thread with nothing else.
findings.fix: Move narrative generation off the tick thread: push a job onto a queue at day rollover and run diary/story generation in a background worker (threading.Thread, asyncio task queue, or sio.start_background_task), emitting the story when done. Alternatively batch the diary calls concurrently with a thread pool to cut the stall to one call's latency.

verdict.justification: The code demonstrably behaves as described. simulation/manager.py:356 gates on `hour == 3 and minute == 0`, then lines 361-362 sequentially call narrative_system.write_agent_diary() for all 6 agents (simulation/config.py:302-337 defines exactly 6), line 363 calls compile_daily_story(), and line 366 emits the story — all inside tick(). Both narrative calls use max_tokens=2048 (narrative_system.py:37, :66) and the diary prompt literally says "Make the entry as complete and long as possible" (narrative_system.py:35). Each call bottoms out in llm_handler.py:33: a synchronous, non-streaming requests.post with NO timeout, so the stall is bounded only by the API (worst case unbounded — the claim if anything understates this). The tick loop in command.py:66-72 is single-threaded and emits 'simulation_state_update' only after tick() returns; a project-wide grep confirms no Thread/start_background_task/async anywhere, so nothing runs during the block: no state updates, frozen agents, stopped sim time. The day-length math is verified: minute += 2 per tick (manager.py:168) and a 0.4s interval (command.py:64) give 720 ticks x 0.4s = 288s = 4.8 min/sim-day, and the 03:00 trigger fires every day (minutes always even; rollover yields 0). Two trivial imprecisions do not rise to PARTIAL: the frontend freezes showing 02:58 (the 03:00 payload built at lines 349-353 is emitted only after the LLM block), and pause/resume handlers do run on the socketio client's receive thread setting simulation_paused — but the flag is only checked between ticks, so the claimed observable (pause has no visible effect during the stall) is correct. Per-call latency figures are hedged estimates consistent with 2048-token-capped generations. Critical severity is fair for a real-time simulation frozen roughly half of wall-clock time per day cycle with an unbounded worst case; aggravating factor on the same path: an HTTPError re-raised from llm_handler.py:38 is caught by command.py:76-78 which breaks the loop, terminating the whole simulation.

findings.title: Daily stories never reach the browser: emit_daily_story fires on a second, never-started SocketIO server inside the command process
findings.description: manager.py:10 does `from app import emit_daily_story`, and tick() calls it at manager.py:366. But AgentManager runs inside command.py (a python-socketio CLIENT process); importing app there executes app.py top-level and constructs a SECOND Flask app + SocketIO server instance (app.py:10-12) that is never started (socketio.run only executes under app.py's __main__ guard, app.py:73-74), has zero connected clients, and no message_queue bridging processes. socketio.emit('new_daily_story', ...) (app.py:39-41) is therefore a silent no-op; the real server the browsers connect to never emits the event and has no relay handler. The frontend listener at static/script.js:95 can never fire and the dynamically created 'All Town Daily Stories' panel stays empty forever — the entire LLM narrative UI is a dead subsystem end-to-end (stories survive only as .txt files on disk). State updates work only because command.py sends them through its socketio CLIENT (sio.emit), which the real server rebroadcasts. The same import coupling means command.py:8 pulls MAP_LAYOUT/PLACES from app.py, executing web-server side effects (file I/O, SocketIO construction) in the sim process; the simulation core cannot be imported or unit-tested without Flask and the static map, map loading lives in the wrong layer, and debug's reloader runs it twice.
findings.fix: Remove `from app import emit_daily_story` from manager.py. Have tick() return the story in its payload (or accept an emit callback) and let command.py sio.emit('new_daily_story', story_data), with a @socketio.on('new_daily_story') rebroadcast handler in app.py mirroring the existing simulation_state_update relay. Alternatively configure a shared message queue (SocketIO(message_queue=...)) or collapse to a single process. Move map loading/PLACES parsing into a shared module (e.g. simulation/world.py) so neither process imports the other.

verdict.justification: Every cited line matches the code and the mechanism is exactly as described. simulation/manager.py:10 does `from app import emit_daily_story`, and tick() calls it at manager.py:366 (inside the reachable `hour == 3 and minute == 0` block at manager.py:356; time advances +2 min/tick from 8:00 so 3:00 is hit every sim day). AgentManager runs in the command process (command.py:7 imports it; command.py:13 is a python-socketio Client; README.md:104/109 document `python app.py` and `python command.py` as two separate processes). Importing app in the command process executes app.py top-level, constructing a second Flask+SocketIO instance (app.py:10-12) with NO message_queue (grep confirms `message_queue` appears nowhere in the repo) that is never started — socketio.run is only under the `__main__` guard (app.py:73-74). emit_daily_story (app.py:39-41) therefore calls socketio.emit('new_daily_story', ...) on a server object with zero connected clients and no bridge to the real server: a silent no-op. The real server process never calls emit_daily_story and has no 'new_daily_story' relay handler (its only handlers are connect/disconnect/command_client_ready/simulation_state_update/pause_simulation/resume_simulation, app.py:43-71). The frontend listener at static/script.js:95 is the only code path that populates DAILY_STORIES in practice (addDailyStory at script.js:265-268 has no callers; the only fetch is /map_data.json at script.js:292), so the dynamically created 'All Town Daily Stories' panel (script.js:75-92) stays empty forever. The contrast claim is also correct: state updates reach browsers only because command.py sends them via its socketio CLIENT (command.py:71) and app.py rebroadcasts (app.py:58-61). Stories survive only as .txt files written by simulation/narrative/narrative_system.py:38-42 and 67-69 (plus an unread in-memory list at manager.py:364). Secondary claims hold too: command.py:8 pulls MAP_LAYOUT/PLACES from app.py, executing map file I/O (app.py:17-26) and SocketIO construction in the sim process; manager.py:10's import means the simulation core cannot be imported without Flask and static/map_data.json; and app.py:74 runs with debug=True, so the Werkzeug reloader re-executes the top-level map loading twice in the server process. Severity Critical is warranted: the LLM narrative UI — the headline feature of a project named 'Story Simulator' — is dead end-to-end and fails silently.

findings.title: Food-emergency branch teleport-eats: agent eats instantly, anywhere, for free — never travels to the cafe and never pays
findings.description: Sequence('Critical: Find Food When Starving') (lines 625-629) has children [IsNeedCritical, PlanPathToEatLocation, ExecuteEat] with no at-location gate, unlike the rest branch which wraps its action behind an IsAtActivityLocation check inside a Selector (line 619). Sequence.tick's while-loop (behavior_tree.py:168-183) runs all three in ONE tick: PlanPathToEatLocation sets state='moving' with destination 'downtown_cafe' and returns SUCCESS (lines 506-507); ExecuteEat then immediately overwrites state to 'doing_action' (line 529), so manager.py:241's movement branch never runs. eat_ticks>=1 on the first tick (lines 533-534), so hunger drops 70 instantly wherever the agent is standing, and the $10 eat_at_cafe cost registered at lines 510-513 is never deducted (ExecuteEat never touches agent.money). The agent then freezes for duration=10 ticks displaying 'Eating at the cafe' — possibly in the middle of a street. Trigger: any agent reaching hunger>=85 (hunger rises 0.25/tick, entities.py:74,82) while energy<70, e.g. one who couldn't afford scheduled meals.
findings.fix: Mirror the rest branch structure: Sequence(IsNeedCritical, Selector(Sequence(IsAtEatLocation, ExecuteEat), PlanPathToEatLocation)) so the agent must physically arrive at the cafe first, and deduct the activity cost inside ExecuteEat before reducing hunger.

verdict.justification: Traced the full path and every claimed step is real. (1) behavior/agent_behaviors.py:625-629 defines Sequence('Critical: Find Food When Starving') = [IsNeedCritical(hunger,85), PlanPathToEatLocation, ExecuteEat] with no at-location gate, unlike the rest branch (615-623) whose Selector (617) gates ExecuteRest behind IsAtActivityLocation (619). (2) behavior/behavior_tree.py:167-186 — Sequence.tick's while-loop advances past each SUCCESS child within the same call (child.reset(); current_child_index+=1; continue at 172-175), so all three children run in one tick. (3) PlanPathToEatLocation (503-515) sets destination_name='downtown_cafe', state='moving', current_activity='eat_at_cafe', registers cost 10 (510-513) and returns SUCCESS; ExecuteEat (528-539) then overwrites state='doing_action' (529), sets action_duration=10 (530) and current_action='Eating at the cafe' (531), increments eat_ticks 0->1 (533), and since eat_ticks>=1 (534) immediately drops hunger by 70 (535) and nulls current_activity (537), returning RUNNING. (4) simulation/manager.py ticks the BT only when state=='idle' (238-239); the subsequent movement branch `if agent.state == 'moving':` (241) is skipped because state is now 'doing_action' — no path is computed, agent.x/y never change, the agent never travels to the cafe. (5) ExecuteEat never touches agent.money, the manager's doing_action block (202-236) only adds work income, and HasEnoughMoney (56-61) only gates the scheduled branch — the $10 is never deducted. (6) The agent then stays frozen 10 ticks (action_duration decrement at manager.py:203, idle+BT reset at 233-235) displaying 'Eating at the cafe' at its current tile, which can be a street tile (agents go idle mid-route at manager.py:275 and 280-282). (7) Trigger is as described: entities.py:74/82 raises hunger 0.25/tick while awake; energy<70 is required because higher-priority branches (IsAgentTired thresholds 95/70 at agent_behaviors.py:611/616) otherwise capture the tick; broke agents skip scheduled meals via HasEnoughMoney failure so hunger>=85 is reachable. Only trivial imprecision: the rest branch's Selector is at line 617 (IsAtActivityLocation at 619), which the claim conflates — this does not alter mechanism or severity. Severity Critical is appropriate for this project: a core survival behavior wholly bypasses travel and payment, corrupting both spatial simulation fidelity and the agent economy.

findings.title: Fresh install per README cannot run the simulator: 'requests' (and socketio client extras) missing, and no requirements.txt exists
findings.description: README.md:87-92 gives the only install instructions: pip install flask flask-socketio python-dotenv plus the analyzer stack (pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn, textblob, networkx, numpy). None of these depends on 'requests', yet simulation/llm_handler.py:4 imports it at module level. Execution path: python command.py -> command.py:7 imports simulation.manager -> manager.py:9 imports simulation.llm_handler -> 'import requests' raises ModuleNotFoundError before anything runs. The python-socketio sync client used by command.py also needs client extras (its engineio polling transport requires 'requests'; 'websocket-client' is needed for websocket upgrade) which flask-socketio does not pull in. On a clean venv the sim process cannot start at all — only 'python app.py' runs with the listed packages. There is no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or lockfile anywhere in the repo.
findings.fix: Add 'requests' and 'python-socketio[client]' (or 'websocket-client') to the README install command, and better, commit a pinned requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml) covering all runtime and analysis dependencies and reference it from the README.

verdict.justification: Every element of the finding checks out against the code and against an empirical clean-venv dependency resolution. (1) README.md:87-92 is the only install guidance in the repo: `pip install flask flask-socketio python-dotenv` plus `pandas matplotlib seaborn scikit-learn textblob networkx numpy`. (2) No dependency manifest exists anywhere: Glob for requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg, Pipfile(.lock), environment.yml/yaml, poetry.lock, uv.lock returned nothing. (3) simulation/llm_handler.py:4 is a module-level `import requests`. (4) The execution path is real: command.py:7 `from simulation.manager import AgentManager` triggers simulation/manager.py:8 (`from simulation.narrative.narrative_system import NarrativeSystem`, whose line 7 imports simulation.llm_handler) and manager.py:9 (`from simulation.llm_handler import LLMHandler`) — either way, llm_handler's `import requests` executes during `python command.py` startup and raises ModuleNotFoundError before sio.connect() is ever reached. (The very first trigger is technically manager.py:8 via narrative_system.py:7 rather than manager.py:9, but manager.py:9 imports it directly too — same mechanism, same traceback endpoint.) (5) Empirical proof that no listed package pulls in requests: `pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report` on the exact README command resolved 40 packages (bidict, blinker, click, colorama, contourpy, cycler, Flask, Flask-SocketIO, ... python-engineio, python-socketio, simple-websocket, ...); `requests` and `websocket-client` are absent. flask-socketio pulls python-socketio/python-engineio (so `import socketio` at command.py:5 succeeds) but not the client extras. (6) The secondary claim about the socketio client is also accurate: site-packages engineio/client.py lines 11-17 wrap `import requests` and `import websocket` in try/except setting them to None, and at connect time (~line 178-181) it errors 'requests package is not installed -- cannot send HTTP requests!' — so even without the llm_handler import, command.py could not connect via polling, and websocket-client is indeed only needed for the websocket upgrade. (7) app.py imports only os, json, flask, flask_socketio and runs fine with the listed packages, as claimed. The only nano-quibbles — the first llm_handler import fires one line earlier than cited, and narrative_analyzer.py (not just app.py) also runs with the listed packages — do not change the mechanism or consequence. Critical severity is appropriate: a user following the documented setup cannot start the simulator process at all, and there is no manifest to fall back on.

findings.title: StatefulSelector never falls back to a sibling on child FAILURE — free-time/social/Idle branches are unreachable and agents freeze during schedule gaps
findings.description: StatefulSelector.tick (lines 129-145) ticks the selected child and, on FAILURE, resets and returns FAILURE without trying any sibling. Combined with the always-first-child selection bug (F08/F09), core_behavior_branch (agent_behaviors.py:602-605) always selects scheduled_activity_branch; when IsScheduledActivity or HasEnoughMoney fails, the whole tree returns FAILURE and free_time_branch (ShouldSocialize, FindAgentToTalkTo, Idle — agent_behaviors.py:579-585) can NEVER execute, so the personality-flavored Idle node never runs. Reachable trigger: alex (workaholic, sleeps 01-06 per manager.py:118-120) has weekday schedule gaps 23:00-01:00 and 06:00-07:00 where _update_agent_schedules sets current_activity=None (manager.py:110-111); IsScheduledActivity fails, the root returns FAILURE, and alex stands frozen with a stale current_goal. Same for diana 06:00-08:00 and fiona weekends 10:00-11:00. The one-on-one conversation subsystem (FindAgentToTalkTo plus the interacting_with rendezvous in manager.py:330-344) is consequently dead code.
findings.fix: In StatefulSelector.tick, when the selected child returns FAILURE, remove it from the candidates and try the next-best child within the same tick (loop until a child returns SUCCESS/RUNNING or all fail), matching standard utility-selector fallback semantics.

verdict.justification: Every element of the claim checks out against the code. (1) Mechanism: behavior/behavior_tree.py StatefulSelector.tick (lines 129-145) ticks exactly one selected child; lines 138-141 handle any non-RUNNING status by resetting selected_child and line 145 returns that status directly — FAILURE propagates with no sibling fallback. (2) Always-first-child selection: _select_best_child (lines 93-111) scores children via simulate_child (lines 113-127), which mutates the simulated outcome only when the child NAME contains "socialize", "work", or "eat". core_behavior_branch's children are named "Follow My Schedule" and "Free Time Activities" (agent_behaviors.py:602-605) — neither contains a keyword, so both simulations return unchanged needs/money, heuristic_function returns 1.0 for both, and the strict `score > best_score` comparison (behavior_tree.py:104) keeps the first child, scheduled_activity_branch, every single tick. (3) Consequence: when IsScheduledActivity (agent_behaviors.py:46, FAILURE if current_activity is None) or HasEnoughMoney (lines 56-61) fails, the Sequence fails, the StatefulSelector returns FAILURE, and the root Selector (lines 608-633, core_behavior_branch is its last child) returns FAILURE — free_time_branch (lines 579-585) and the personality-flavored Idle node (lines 546-566) are structurally unreachable. (4) Reachable triggers verified in simulation/config.py and manager.py: alex is 'workaholic' (config.py:304) → sleeps 01-06 (manager.py:118-120) with office_worker_extrovert weekday schedule spanning 8:00-23:00 (config.py:82-91), leaving gaps at 23:00-01:00 and 06:00-08:00 (the claim says 06:00-07:00; the real gap is even wider since the schedule starts at 8, so the claimed window is a true subset); diana is 'fitness_enthusiast' → sleeps 22-06, student schedule starts at 8 → gap 06:00-08:00; fiona is 'lazy' → sleeps until 10, lazy_sleeper weekend schedule starts at 11 → gap 10:00-11:00. In those gaps _update_agent_schedules sets current_activity=None (manager.py:110-111), and manager.tick (line 238-239) just ticks the BT for idle agents — a FAILURE return changes nothing, so the agent stands idle with its stale current_goal (entities.py never clears it), interrupted only if the higher-priority rest (energy>=70) or hunger (>=85) branches fire; at alex's post-sleep 06:00-08:00 gap energy is ~0, so a genuine multi-hour freeze is reachable. (5) Dead code: grep confirms FindAgentToTalkTo exists only inside free_time_branch, and agent_behaviors.py:159 is the sole producer of destination_name="agent_*", which is the only way to reach the moving-with-interacting_with rendezvous at manager.py:330-344 (ExecuteActivity's park socializing sets state='interacting' directly, never 'moving'), so that rendezvous path is dead as claimed — the finding correctly scopes this to FindAgentToTalkTo-initiated conversations, not park socializing. Severity Major is appropriate: no crash, but an entire designed subsystem (spontaneous one-on-one socializing and personality idle behaviors) can never execute and agents visibly stall for hours of sim time. The one micro-imprecision (06:00-07:00 vs the actual 06:00-08:00 gap) understates rather than overstates the defect and does not affect mechanism or severity, so CONFIRMED rather than PARTIAL.

findings.title: heuristic_function maps every non-negative outcome to exactly 1.0 — utility selection degenerates to fixed first-child priority
findings.description: normalized_score = 1/(1+max(0,-score)) equals 1.0 for ALL score>=0, so any beneficial or neutral outcome ties at exactly 1.0 and the strict '>' comparison in _select_best_child (line 104) keeps the first child; ordering exists only among harmful (negative) outcomes. In free_time_branch, 'Try to socialize' scores raw +20 which still normalizes to 1.0, tying with Idle's 1.0 — first child wins again. Selection is therefore ALWAYS the first child, identical to a plain priority Selector, and the utility-selection machinery adds nothing.
findings.fix: Replace the normalization with a monotonic squashing that preserves ordering for positive scores (e.g. sigmoid(score/k)) or compare raw scores directly; break ties deliberately, or keep priority order intentionally and delete the dead heuristic machinery.

verdict.justification: Every element of the claim is verified in code. (1) behavior/behavior_tree.py:28 — normalized_score = 1/(1+max(0,-score)) returns exactly 1.0 for all score >= 0; ordering survives only among negative scores. (2) Lines 96/104 — best_score starts at -1 and the strict 'score > best_score' comparison keeps the first child on ties. (3) Line 101 shows selection uses simulate_child (lines 113-127), which only decreases needs (socialize: social-20, eat: hunger-30) or increases money (work: +10); heuristic_function scores (initial-final)*weight + money_change*0.5, so raw scores are always >= 0 and EVERY child normalizes to exactly 1.0 — the first child always wins in both StatefulSelector instances. findings.title: simulate_child never calls child.simulate() and keyword-matches node names that never match — the entire lookahead subsystem is behaviorally dead

findings.title: Selector.simulate returns after simulating only the first child, and is_running bookkeeping is broken — the RUNNING-resume machinery never engages
findings.description: Three framework defects: (1) Selector.simulate (lines 78-81) is `for child in self.children: return child.simulate(...)` — an unconditional return inside the loop simulates only children[0], making selector lookahead wrong by construction. (2) Selector.tick (lines 71-76) returns RUNNING without setting self.is_running=True, and leaf actions returning RUNNING (ExecuteActivity, ExecuteRest, ExecuteEat) never set is_running either, so a StatefulSelector parent checking selected_child.is_running (line 130) would re-select instead of resuming. (3) In the real wiring these are latent because the resume path is dead code: RUNNING is only returned when the agent simultaneously leaves the 'idle' state, the BT is only ticked while idle (manager.py:238-239), and the manager resets the whole tree when every action/interaction ends or on arrival (manager.py:231, 235, 347) — so the is_running=True branch can never be taken and StatefulSelector 'commitment' is illusory (every tick is a fresh selection).
findings.fix: Set is_running=True whenever a node returns RUNNING (Selector and leaf actions), define real selector simulation semantics (simulate the child most likely to run, or best-case over children) instead of returning on the first iteration, and decide whether cross-tick RUNNING resumption is wanted — if so stop resetting the BT on every action completion in manager.tick; if not, delete the is_running/selected_child resume machinery.

findings.title: Rest branch keys off scheduler-owned current_activity: agents nap instantly at the wrong place, or pace forever and never actually rest
findings.description: The rest branch (lines 615-624) reuses IsAtActivityLocation, which checks the location of agent.current_activity — a field the scheduler owns. Two failure modes. (a) Wrong-place nap: on the first tired tick current_activity is still the scheduled activity (e.g. work_at_office), so if the agent is at work the check passes and ExecuteRest fires instantly at the office, restoring 70 energy and clearing current_activity — silently cancelling work. (b) Pacing livelock: PlanPathToRestLocation sets current_activity='take_a_short_rest' and state='moving' (lines 456-459), but arrival sets state='idle' and resets the BT (manager.py:346-347), and on the next tick _update_agent_schedules (manager.py:189; line 92 skips only 'interacting'/'moving') overwrites current_activity with the scheduled activity or None BEFORE the BT re-ticks. IsAtActivityLocation therefore never sees 'take_a_short_rest', fails, and PlanPathToRestLocation re-plans to the same rest_location — the agent walks to another cell of the same place (its own cell is in claimed_spots, manager.py:196/263), arrives, and loops. Because this branch outranks the schedule branch, a tired agent also never executes sleep_at_home (e.g. alex tired at the bar at 23:00 paces in the park all night), energy declining only ~0.8 on the single idle tick per pace cycle.
findings.fix: Introduce a dedicated per-agent rest intent (e.g. agent.rest_location) with an IsAtRestLocation condition keyed off it, or exempt BT-initiated activities ('take_a_short_rest', 'eat_at_cafe') from the _update_agent_schedules overwrite; and don't clear current_activity as a side effect of ExecuteRest.

A tired agent (energy need >= 70, line 616) standing at its scheduled location (e.g. work_at_office -> business_office, config.py:203) passes the check, and ExecuteRest (lines 478-490) fires instantly there: rest_ticks is pre-initialized (entities.py:46) so the >= 1 branch runs on the first tick, cutting the energy need by 70 and nulling current_activity. findings.title: Exhaustion emergency branch has no sleep action: exhausted agents pace at home for hours, shadowing rest, food, and scheduled sleep
findings.description: 'Emergency: Go Home When Exhausted' (lines 610-613) is the root's first child: IsAgentTired(threshold=95) then PlanPathToHome, which unconditionally sets state='moving' toward home and returns SUCCESS (lines 433-438) — there is no rest/sleep action in the branch. Energy only decreases when current_activity=='sleep_at_home', which _is_sleep_time (manager.py:113-126) gates by hour. Once the agent is home with energy>=95 outside its sleep window, every idle BT tick re-triggers PlanPathToHome; the manager picks another unclaimed home cell (manager.py:156-161; the agent's own cell is claimed via line 196), the agent walks there, arrives, resets, and repeats — re-planning 'Emergency path home' every tick for hours, spamming logs and doing nothing. Because the branch returns SUCCESS it also shadows the 'Urgent: Rest' branch, the food branch, and scheduled sleep_at_home. For alex (workaholic, sleep 01:00-06:00), hitting energy 95 mid-day means pacing at home for many sim-hours, skipping all scheduled activities, until the sleep window passively rescues him.
findings.fix: Add a terminal action to the emergency sequence: gate with an at-home condition and execute an ExecuteSleep/deep-rest action that actually reduces energy (analogous to ExecuteRest), or let critical exhaustion override the _is_sleep_time schedule gate, instead of returning SUCCESS from path-planning alone.

Mechanism confirmation: behavior/agent_behaviors.py:608-613 makes the emergency Sequence (IsAgentTired threshold=95 at line 611, PlanPathToHome at 612) the first child of the stateless root Selector (behavior_tree.py:71-76), and PlanPathToHome (lines 433-438) only sets state='moving' and returns SUCCESS — no energy-reducing action. Passive energy decrease requires current_activity=='sleep_at_home' (entities.py:81-97), gated by _is_sleep_time (manager.py:113-126, workaholic alex = 01:00-06:00). Because manager.py:196 claims the agent's own cell, _get_agent_home_target (manager.py:156-161) always returns a different home cell, so the agent walks, arrives (manager.py:345-347, idle + BT reset), and re-triggers on the next idle tick (238-239). Empirical injection test (headless run of AgentManager, alex energy forced to 96 at day-0 10:00): stuck for 457 ticks = 15.2 sim-hours, 146 PlanPathToHome firings, 439/457 ticks confined to the 9-cell north_houses block across 21 positions, hunger pinned at 100 with zero ExecuteEat, all scheduled activities (work, lunch, gym, dinner, socialize, nightlife) skipped, rescued only at 01:14 by sleep-window passive decay — exactly as described, confirming the shadowing of the rest, food, and scheduled-sleep branches. findings.title: ExecuteActivity re-charges the full activity cost every ~8 ticks for the same schedule slot, draining agents' money several times per activity and spamming logs all night
findings.description: ExecuteActivity deducts the FULL activity cost and sets action_duration=8 ticks (16 sim-minutes) each time it starts (lines 244-247, duration default at :180). When the action expires the manager sets the agent idle and resets the BT (manager.py:225-235); next tick the schedule slot is still active, so the tree re-runs IsScheduledActivity -> HasEnoughMoney -> IsAtActivityLocation -> ExecuteActivity and charges the full cost AGAIN. A 2-hour dinner_at_cafe slot (config.py:97, cost $20 at config.py:227) is charged ~6-7 times (~$130-140) against starting money of 100-150 (entities.py:39); nightlife_at_bar ($60/hour, config.py:270) costs ~$225 — while wages accrue at only 0.5-0.8 per tick (manager.py:218-223). The config's costs are therefore not per-visit prices as written; agents go broke within the first sim-day, HasEnoughMoney starts failing, and — via the no-fallback bug (F07) — they stand frozen logging 'I can't afford...' every tick. The same expiry loop makes sleep_at_home re-execute every ~9 ticks all night, appending 'I've arrived at the home...' (agent_behaviors.py:255) roughly 200 times per agent per night — flushing the 50-entry log cap (entities.py:64-65) and bloating the memory stream that feeds the diaries.
findings.fix: Charge the cost once per schedule slot (track (activity, slot) or last_paid_activity on the agent and skip the deduction on re-entry), or set action_duration to span the remaining schedule window instead of a fixed 8 ticks; suppress the arrival log when re-executing the same continuing activity.

findings.title: ExecuteActivity's park branch mutates the partner agent directly mid-tick — order-dependent desync and needs-model bypass
findings.description: The socialize_at_park branch (lines 219-239) directly rewrites another agent's state: partner.state='interacting', partner.interacting_with, partner.action_duration, and partner.needs['social']=0 (lines 231-236), plus agent.needs['social']=0 (line 229). Because manager.tick processes agents in shuffled order (manager.py:191-192), a partner processed later in the same tick immediately decrements the freshly-assigned action_duration (manager.py:202-203) while the initiator starts decrementing next tick — the partner finishes one tick earlier and force-idles/resets the initiator mid-interaction (manager.py:226-231); a partner already processed this tick can be double-moved or skip decrements. The hard needs['social']=0 also bypasses the calibrated -60 adjustment in _update_needs_for_activity (line 351), making the direct-mutation path inconsistent with the rest of the needs model. There is no event system mediating cross-agent effects.
findings.fix: Mediate interactions through the manager or an event queue and apply symmetric state changes at a single point (reuse the manager-side interaction setup at manager.py:330-340); start countdowns from the following tick for both parties, and reuse _update_needs_for_activity's -60 social adjustment instead of zeroing needs directly.

verdict.justification: The cited mechanics are real but the failure impact is overstated and one claimed effect is false. CONFIRMED facts: (1) behavior/agent_behaviors.py:224-236 directly mutates the partner (partner.state='interacting', partner.interacting_with, partner.action_duration, partner.needs['social']=0 at 231-236; agent.needs['social']=0 at 229). (2) manager.py:191-192 shuffles the processing order; because the initiator's BT runs inside its own 'idle' branch iteration (manager.py:238-239), the initiator skips the decrement that tick, while a partner later in the shuffle immediately decrements the freshly assigned action_duration at manager.py:202-203 — so the partner reaches 0 one tick before the initiator and the teardown at 225-235 force-idles/resets the initiator with 1 tick remaining. (3) The park branch returns RUNNING at line 239 before _update_needs_for_activity, so the -60 social adjustment (line 351) never applies on this path. REFUTED/OVERSTATED parts: (a) "double-moved" has no code path — the mutation never repositions the partner; an already-processed partner merely skips one decrement, which yields the correct lockstep countdown from the next tick (benign). (b) The "desync" is transient and self-correcting: manager.py:226-235 is the intentional mutual teardown, and both agents end in a consistent idle state; the only observable effects are a conversation one tick shorter than nominal for one party (~50% of park interactions) and an asymmetric "Finished my conversation" log. No stuck state, crash, or lasting inconsistency. (c) needs['social']=0 carries an explicit "# Reset social need" comment — a deliberate choice differing only modestly from max(0, x-60). (d) The proposed fix's premise is wrong: the manager's own interaction setup (manager.py:330-340) performs the identical mid-tick direct mutation and duration assignment and is subject to the same shuffled-order off-by-one at 202-203, so the pattern is codebase-wide, not branch-specific, and "reuse manager.py:330-340" would not remove it. Real code smell + minor timing asymmetry, but Major severity and the desync/double-move framing do not hold.
verdict.corrected_title: Park socialize branch mutates partner mid-tick, causing a shuffle-order one-tick countdown asymmetry and skipping the standard -60 social-need adjustment
verdict.corrected_description: ExecuteActivity's socialize_at_park branch (behavior/agent_behaviors.py:219-239) directly rewrites the partner's state (lines 231-236) and hard-resets both agents' needs['social'] to 0 (lines 229, 236) instead of applying the calibrated -60 adjustment in _update_needs_for_activity (line 351), which is unreachable on this path because the branch returns RUNNING early. Because manager.tick processes agents in shuffled order (manager.py:191-192) and the initiator's BT runs in its own iteration, a partner processed later in the same tick decrements the freshly assigned action_duration immediately (manager.py:202-203), finishing one tick early and triggering the mutual teardown (manager.py:225-235) that idles the initiator with one tick of duration left — the initiator's interaction is ~1 tick shorter than nominal in about half of park interactions and it never emits the "Finished my conversation" log. The state remains fully consistent afterward (the teardown resets both parties), a partner processed earlier simply starts its countdown next tick in correct lockstep, and no "double-move" occurs. The same mid-tick direct-mutation/duration-assignment pattern exists in the manager's own interaction setup (manager.py:330-340), so this is a codebase-wide design pattern rather than a branch-specific desync; impact is limited to a one-tick timing asymmetry, asymmetric logging, and a needs-model inconsistency that the code comments mark as intentional ("Reset social need").

findings.title: One-sided interaction teardown breaks the interacting_with invariant: dangling references cause frozen partners, spurious interactions, and conversation hijacking
findings.description: Several code paths mutate one side of an interaction without the other. (1) The 22:00 forced-idle for socialize_at_park (manager.py:87-91) sets state='idle' and current_activity=None even mid-'interacting' but does NOT clear interacting_with/action_duration nor release the partner — the partner stays frozen 'interacting' until its own timer expires, at which point manager.py:227-231 force-resets the first agent AGAIN, clobbering whatever it started since (including yanking it out of a NEW conversation with a third agent, leaving that third agent dangling too). (2) Path-failure branches (manager.py:273-282, 'no path'/'no space') set state='idle' but never clear interacting_with; the stale ID persists, and the NEXT time the agent completes any walk (e.g. to work) manager.py:330 sees interacting_with set and starts a spurious interaction with that agent. (3) When A arrives while B (mutually targeting A) is mid-walk, manager.py:333-335 flips B to 'interacting' without clearing B's partial path/path_index; after the chat, B's BT plans a new destination but manager.py:245 sees the leftover non-empty path and walks B to the stale old target first. All of this depends on the shuffled processing order (manager.py:192), so behavior differs run to run.
findings.fix: Centralize a break_interaction(a) helper that symmetrically clears state, interacting_with, action_duration, and path on BOTH agents and resets both BTs; call it from the forced-idle, path-failure, and duration-expiry paths. Clear path/path_index whenever an agent leaves 'moving' for any reason.

verdict.justification: The core invariant violation is real and the cited lines are accurate: manager.py:87-91 force-idles a socialize_at_park agent at hour>=22 even mid-'interacting' (the state guard at line 92 comes after) without clearing interacting_with/action_duration/path; manager.py:273-282 set idle without clearing interacting_with; manager.py:333-335 flip the partner to 'interacting' without clearing its path, which manager.py:245 later resumes. The demonstrable, nightly-reachable consequence (every schedule template has (20,22) socialize_at_park; 8-15-tick conversations routinely span 22:00): both partners keep stale MUTUAL interacting_with, and when one completes its next walk, manager.py:330-340 starts a spurious cross-town "conversation" — line 332's `other_agent.interacting_with == agent.id` fires even when the partner is 'moving' (frozen mid-street with a partial path) or 'doing_action' (yanked out of sleep). However, two of the three claimed mechanisms are wrong. (a) The "partner stays frozen 'interacting' until its own timer expires, then 227-231 force-resets the first agent AGAIN / yanks it out of a NEW conversation with a third agent" chain cannot occur: park interactions (agent_behaviors.py:204-236, the only live interaction-creation path) require BOTH partners to have current_activity=='socialize_at_park', and the unshuffled schedule loop at manager.py:85 force-idles both in the same pass; once idle, line 202's gate stops the countdown so the 225-235 expiry never fires for them, and line 332's guard blocks stealing an agent already interacting with a third party (lines 342-344 run instead). (b) Claim (3)'s trigger — mutual FindAgentToTalkTo targeting — is unreachable dead code: StatefulSelector._select_best_child (behavior_tree.py:93-111) scores both core children ("Follow My Schedule", "Free Time Activities") at exactly 1.0 (simulate_child keyword-matches child names, neither matches; heuristic_function line 28 clamps non-negative scores to 1.0) and strict '>' keeps the first child, so the free-time branch — the only setter of interacting_with with state='moving' — never runs; consequently claim (2)'s path-failure branch is never an independent source of staleness either (it merely fails to clean staleness created by the force-idle). (c) The shuffle at line 192 is not load-bearing — the force-idle hits both partners deterministically. The surviving defect (nightly conversation truncation, spurious frozen cross-town interactions hijacking sleeping/walking agents, corrupted goals/logs feeding the LLM narratives, stale-path resumption) is a recurring user-visible correctness bug in the core loop, so Major severity stands.
verdict.corrected_title: 22:00 socialize_at_park force-idle leaves stale mutual interacting_with (and paths) uncleaned, causing spurious cross-town interactions that hijack sleeping/walking partners
verdict.corrected_description: The 22:00 forced-idle for socialize_at_park (manager.py:87-91) runs even while an agent is 'interacting' (the state guard at line 92 comes after it) and sets state='idle'/current_activity=None without clearing interacting_with, action_duration, or path. Because both partners of a park interaction necessarily have current_activity=='socialize_at_park' (agent_behaviors.py:204-236 is the only live interaction-creation path) and the schedule loop (manager.py:85) covers all agents in one pass, BOTH are force-idled the same tick — so no partner stays frozen waiting for its timer (once idle, line 202's gate stops the countdown and the 225-235 expiry never fires). The real damage is the stale MUTUAL interacting_with left on both agents: when either later completes any walk (e.g., home to sleep), manager.py:330-340 starts a spurious interaction because line 332's `other_agent.interacting_with == agent.id` check passes even when the partner is 'moving' or 'doing_action' — the partner is yanked out of sleep or frozen mid-street for 15-25 ticks in a fake cross-town "conversation", with goals/logs overwritten (polluting the LLM daily narratives). Lines 333-335 also do not clear the hijacked partner's partial path/path_index, so after the fake chat manager.py:245 resumes the stale path before any new destination. The path-failure branches (manager.py:273-282) likewise never clear interacting_with, though they only preserve — not create — the staleness, since FindAgentToTalkTo (the only setter of interacting_with with state='moving') is unreachable: StatefulSelector._select_best_child (behavior_tree.py:93-111, 28) ties all non-negative scores at 1.0 and strict '>' always keeps the first child ("Follow My Schedule"), so the free-time/socialize branch and the "agent_" destination handling (manager.py:250-255) are dead code. Fix: a symmetric break_interaction helper clearing state, interacting_with, action_duration, and path on both agents (called from the forced-idle and expiry paths), plus clearing path/path_index whenever an agent leaves 'moving'.

findings.title: Arrival-triggered interaction never checks the target is still nearby — conversations start across the map
findings.description: When an agent finishes its path with interacting_with set (manager.py:327-340), the only conditions checked are `other_agent.state == 'idle' or other_agent.interacting_with == agent.id`. The path target was computed once, adjacent to the target's position at planning time (manager.py:250-255); the target is never reserved and keeps acting during the multi-tick walk (FindAgentToTalkTo only requires it to be idle at selection time, behavior/agent_behaviors.py:139-169). If the target has since walked anywhere else and happens to be idle again on arrival, both agents are put into 'interacting' (manager.py:333-340) despite being arbitrarily far apart — the UI shows two agents chatting from opposite sides of town, and the target is frozen in place for 15-25 ticks wherever it stands.
findings.fix: On arrival, verify adjacency (e.g. Chebyshev distance <= 1-2) to other_agent before starting the interaction; otherwise either replan toward the target's new position or abandon (state='idle', clear interacting_with, reset the BT).

verdict.justification: The claimed mechanism is demonstrably present. FindAgentToTalkTo (behavior/agent_behaviors.py:139-169) selects a target that is merely idle and within abs(dx)<6/abs(dy)<6 at selection time, mutating only the walker (lines 158-162) — the target is never reserved and its BT keeps running, so it can walk anywhere during the multi-tick approach. The walk destination is computed once at planning time from the target's then-current position via _find_adjacent_spot (manager.py:250-255, gated by the path-is-empty check at line 245), and the blocked-path replanning branch (manager.py:291-303) does not handle "agent_" destinations at all, so a blocked walker simply waits while staying 'moving', letting the target travel even farther. On arrival (manager.py:327-344) the only gate is line 332: `other_agent and (other_agent.state == 'idle' or other_agent.interacting_with == agent.id)` — a repo-wide grep confirms no adjacency/distance check exists anywhere in this flow. Lines 333-340 then set both agents to 'interacting' with action_duration = random.randint(15, 25), freezing the target in place wherever it stands (interacting agents only decrement duration, manager.py:202-236). The UI shows both agents' speech bubbles at their real, distant positions (static/script.js:143). Nothing clears the walker's interacting_with mid-walk (clears exist only at manager.py:230/234/344); indeed, pathfinding-failure and no-space branches (manager.py:273-282) leave interacting_with set while going idle, so the walker can even start the "conversation" upon arriving at a completely unrelated later destination — the root cause is, if anything, slightly worse than described. "Arbitrarily far apart" is a fair worst case on the 30x23 map given the unbounded blocked-wait behavior. Severity Major is appropriate: visible correctness failure in the core social loop with false narrative logs, but no crash or data corruption. Cited line numbers (manager.py:330, 327-340, 250-255; agent_behaviors.py:139-169) all check out exactly.

findings.title: Overnight schedule windows like (22,1) can never trigger — party/nightlife config is dead
findings.description: _update_agent_schedules matches activities with `if start_hour <= hour < end_hour` (manager.py:104-105); for wrap-around windows this is unsatisfiable — `22 <= hour < 1` is false for every hour 0-23. Three configured windows are affected (verified programmatically by iterating SCHEDULE_TEMPLATES): config.py:99 office_worker_extrovert weekends (22,1) party_at_bar; config.py:137 cafe_worker_social weekends (22,1) nightlife_at_bar; config.py:186 workaholic_ambitious weekdays (22,1) party_at_bar. Affected agents silently get current_activity=None at 22:00-00:59 and drop into free-time idling instead of going to the bar — the configured nightlife economy/social behavior never happens, which also skews the LLM diaries and the analyzer's social-behavior metrics. Note when fixing: the sleep check runs first (manager.py:99, _is_sleep_time at 113-126), so e.g. a normal sleeper asleep from 23:00 should still sleep through most of a fixed window — the wrap-around fix must coexist with that precedence.
findings.fix: Handle wrap-around in the comparison — `matched = (start <= hour < end) if start < end else (hour >= start or hour < end)` — or split wrapping slots into (22,24) and (0,1) entries in config.py, and audit each (22,1) window against the owning agent's sleep interval.

verdict.justification: The defect is real and behaves exactly as described. simulation/manager.py:104-105 matches schedule windows with `if start_hour <= hour < end_hour:` with no wrap-around handling; for (22,1) this is unsatisfiable for all hours 0-23 (verified programmatically: all three wrap windows match zero hours). The three cited windows exist at exactly the cited lines: config.py:99 (office_worker_extrovert weekends, party_at_bar), config.py:137 (cafe_worker_social weekends, nightlife_at_bar), config.py:186 (workaholic_ambitious weekdays, party_at_bar), and grep confirms manager.py:95/104 is the only code that consumes schedule_template. On no match, manager.py:110-111 sets current_activity=None; the behavior tree cannot reach bar activities without it (IsScheduledActivity gate at behavior/agent_behaviors.py:46; the free-time branch at 579-585 only socializes or idles), so party_at_bar never occurs for any agent. Sleep precedence is as the finding states (manager.py:99, _is_sleep_time 113-126): Alex (workaholic, sleeps 1-6) is awake for the full weekend 22:00-00:59 window and idles instead of partying; Charlie (normal sleeper 23-8) loses only the 22:00 hour, a nuance the finding itself correctly anticipates in its fix note. Two minor imprecisions do not change the verdict: (1) the workaholic_ambitious template is not assigned to any agent in AGENT_CONFIG, so the config.py:186 window is dead config with no live-agent impact (only Alex and Charlie are behaviorally affected); (2) nightlife_at_bar is not entirely dead — Alex's weekday (22,23) window at config.py:90 does trigger — only the wrap-window instances are dead, which is what the finding's title scopes itself to. The downstream claim is plausible: narrative_analyzer.py performs behavioral-keyword/social analysis over LLM diaries. Major severity is appropriate for a silently-dead configured behavior affecting 2 of 6 agents plus the economy sink (activity costs 50/60).

findings.title: Memory streams grow unbounded and weekday-name timestamps make week-2 diaries re-ingest week-1 memories
findings.description: Every Agent.add_log call creates a Memory with timestamp=f"{day_of_week}" — just 'Monday', no date or day index (entities.py:67-69) — and appends it to memory_stream.memories, which is never pruned: AgentMemoryStream.reset_daily_memories (memory.py:39-40) has zero callers anywhere in the repo (grep-verified), and NarrativeSystem.reset_agent_diaries, which manager.py:365 calls nightly, is an explicit no-op 'pass' (narrative_system.py:72-75). get_memories_for_day filters with m.timestamp.startswith(day) (memory.py:36-37), so on day 8 the diary for 'Monday' (narrative_system.py:24) returns BOTH Mondays' memories: week-old events are presented as today's, and by week N each weekday diary prompt contains N days' worth of bullet lines. Agents log dozens-to-hundreds of entries per day (decision logs, arrival/blocked logs, nightly sleep re-execution spam), so both the in-RAM list and the 03:00 LLM prompt grow linearly forever — escalating token cost until the model context is exceeded, at which point diary generation fails and (via F01) kills the sim. agent.log is capped at 50 entries (entities.py:64-65), which protects the UI payload but not the memory stream.
findings.fix: Timestamp memories with the absolute day index (e.g. f"Day {day_index} {day_of_week}"), filter by day_index so identically-named weekdays can never collide, and call reset_daily_memories (or trim/summarize to the last N days) for each agent after the 03:00 diary/story generation in manager.tick().

verdict.justification: Every element of the claim is verified by direct line citation. (1) entities.py:68 creates each Memory with timestamp=f"{day_of_week}" — just the weekday name, no date/day index — and entities.py:69 appends it to memory_stream. (2) The stream is append-only: AgentMemoryStream.reset_daily_memories (memory.py:39-40) has zero callers anywhere in executed code (grep confirms only its definition plus a mention in docs/v2_upgrade/audit_workflow.js documentation). (3) The nightly cleanup hook manager.py:365 calls NarrativeSystem.reset_agent_diaries, whose body is literally `pass` (narrative_system.py:72-75), so nothing is ever pruned. (4) manager.py:175 increments day_index unbounded and manager.py:187 maps it to day_of_week via modulo-7; the 03:00 diary block (manager.py:356-362) passes prev_day_name = days[prev_day_index % 7] to write_agent_diary, which fetches memories via get_memories_for_day(day_name) (narrative_system.py:24) using m.timestamp.startswith(day) (memory.py:36-37). Since week-2 Monday memories also carry timestamp "Monday", the Day-8 Monday diary prompt (narrative_system.py:32 joins ALL matches as bullet lines) contains both Mondays' memories, and each weekday's prompt grows by one full day of memories per week — linear unbounded growth of both RAM and LLM prompt. No weekday name is a prefix of another, so the collision is exactly the same-weekday-across-weeks case claimed. (5) Log volume is realistic: behavior_tree.py:109 logs a decision entry on every StatefulSelector re-selection, and completed actions reset to idle (manager.py:225-236) causing repeated decide/head-home/arrive log cycles overnight (agent_behaviors.py:401, 255), plus blocked/no-space logs (manager.py:289, 282); entities.py:63-65 caps only agent.log at 50, not the memory stream. (6) The kill-the-sim link holds: generate_narrative raises on HTTP error (llm_handler.py:33-39), manager.tick has no try/except around the 03:00 block, and command.py:76-78 catches the exception and breaks the simulation loop. Only trivial softening: gpt-4.1-mini's ~1M context makes actual context exhaustion a long-horizon endpoint, but the finding frames it as the limit of linear growth, and the immediate defects (cross-week memory contamination from Day 8 onward, ever-growing token cost) are stated accurately. Severity Major is appropriate.

findings.title: _select_best_child logs an 'I've decided to...' entry on essentially every idle tick, flooding the 50-entry agent log and the memory stream that feeds the LLM diaries
findings.description: StatefulSelector.tick only reuses selected_child when selected_child.is_running is True (line 130), but in practice every RUNNING action moves the agent out of 'idle' and the manager resets the whole tree when the action ends (manager.py:231, 235, 276, 347), so _select_best_child runs on essentially EVERY idle BT tick (every 0.4s real time, manager.py:238-239). Each call logs "I've decided to: ..." (line 109) via agent.add_log, which both pushes real events out of the 50-entry agent.log (entities.py:62-65) and appends a Memory to the per-day memory_stream (entities.py:66-69, memory.py:33-34) — thousands of identical entries per agent per sim-day polluting the diary/story LLM input. IsAgentTired similarly logs on every successful evaluation (agent_behaviors.py:33) — every tick during the tiredness livelocks — and HasEnoughMoney logs on every failure (agent_behaviors.py:60) — every tick when broke.
findings.fix: Log the decision only when the selection changes (track the previously selected child), move condition-node logging (IsAgentTired, HasEnoughMoney) to the point where the resulting action actually starts, or rate-limit/deduplicate consecutive identical entries in Agent.add_log.

verdict.justification: The mechanism is exactly as described. (1) behavior_tree.py:93-111: _select_best_child always finds a best_child (best_score starts at -1 and heuristic_function at lines 28-29 returns 1/(1+max(0,-score)) > 0), so line 109 logs "I've decided to: ..." on every call. (2) The reuse branch at behavior_tree.py:130 is effectively dead across ticks: the only RUNNING-returning nodes (ExecuteActivity agent_behaviors.py:239/260, ExecuteRest :490, ExecuteEat :539) all first set agent.state to 'doing_action'/'interacting' (:224, :246, :479, :529); the manager only ticks the BT when state == 'idle' (manager.py:238-239) and calls behavior_tree.reset() before the agent is idle again (manager.py:231, 235, 276, 347), which clears selected_child (behavior_tree.py:153-155); for SUCCESS/FAILURE the selector clears selected_child itself (behavior_tree.py:138-140). So _select_best_child runs and logs on every idle BT tick, at the 0.4s loop interval (command.py:64, 72). Continuous 1-log-per-tick (sometimes 2-per-tick) scenarios exist: unscheduled gaps (core always selects "Follow My Schedule" due to the score tie and strict > at behavior_tree.py:104, then IsScheduledActivity fails, agent stays idle), waiting alone at the park (ExecuteActivity returns SUCCESS at agent_behaviors.py:216 leaving the agent idle), and broke agents (line 109 plus HasEnoughMoney failure log at agent_behaviors.py:60 every tick for the whole scheduled block). (3) Consequences confirmed: add_log caps the visible log at 50 entries (entities.py:62-65) and unconditionally appends a Memory (entities.py:66-69, memory.py:33-34); the diary prompt embeds every same-weekday memory (narrative_system.py:24, 32), and reset_daily_memories (memory.py:39) is never called anywhere (reset_agent_diaries is a no-op, narrative_system.py:72-75), so spam accumulates across weeks. (4) Side claims verified: IsAgentTired logs on every successful evaluation (agent_behaviors.py:31-34, used at thresholds 95 and 70 in the root selector, agent_behaviors.py:611, 616); HasEnoughMoney logs on every failed evaluation (agent_behaviors.py:56-61). One minor quantitative caveat that does not affect the verdict or severity: "thousands of identical entries per agent per sim-day" overstates the per-day count — a sim-day is 720 manager ticks (minute += 2 at manager.py:168), so line 109 is hard-capped at 720/day, realistically a few hundred (worst case ~900 total spam/day for a broke agent counting the paired HasEnoughMoney entries); "thousands" in a single diary prompt is reached only after multiple sim-weeks via the never-purged memory stream. The 50-entry UI log and LLM diary pollution effects are real, so Major severity stands.
verdict.corrected_description: StatefulSelector.tick only reuses selected_child when selected_child.is_running is True (behavior_tree.py:130), but every RUNNING action node sets agent.state to 'doing_action'/'interacting' (agent_behaviors.py:224/246/479/529) so the BT is never re-ticked while a child is RUNNING (manager.py:238-239 ticks only idle agents), and the manager resets the whole tree when the action/movement ends (manager.py:231, 235, 276, 347). Consequently _select_best_child runs on essentially every idle BT tick (every 0.4s real time, command.py:64/72) and always logs "I've decided to: ..." Each entry both pushes real events out of the 50-entry agent.log (entities.py:62-65) and appends a Memory to the never-purged memory_stream (entities.py:66-69, memory.py:33-34; reset_daily_memories is never called). Hundreds of identical entries per agent per sim-day (hard cap 720 ticks/day; ~900/day worst case counting paired HasEnoughMoney failure logs) pollute the diary/story LLM prompts (narrative_system.py:24, 32), accumulating into the thousands across sim-weeks since same-weekday memories are never cleared. findings.title: Per-agent rest/eat data is written into the shared global ACTIVITY_DATA dict via world_state — concurrent agents clobber each other's entries
findings.description: PlanPathToRestLocation writes agent-specific data into world_state['activity_data']['take_a_short_rest'] = {location: <this agent's choice>, ...} (lines 460-463); world_state['activity_data'] IS the module-level ACTIVITY_DATA dict (manager.py:55), shared by all agents and permanently mutated. If agent A rests at central_park and agent B then plans a rest at downtown_cafe, the single global entry is overwritten, so A's IsAtActivityLocation lookup for 'take_a_short_rest' (line 81) points at B's location — agent A is validated against agent B's rest spot. PlanPathToEatLocation does the same at lines 510-513 (harmless today only because its location is constant). The impact is currently masked by the rest-livelock bug (F11: the BT never observes 'take_a_short_rest' at check time), but any fix to that bug will expose this cross-agent corruption.
findings.fix: Store per-agent transient activity data on the agent (e.g. agent.dynamic_activity = {'location': ..., 'cost': ...}) or a scoped blackboard, and have IsAtActivityLocation consult it — never write agent-specific entries into shared world config.

verdict.justification: Every claimed element is verifiable in the code. (1) Sharing: simulation/manager.py:55 sets world_state['activity_data'] to the module-level ACTIVITY_DATA dict (imported at manager.py:6 from simulation/config.py:201) by direct reference — no copy — and the single world_state is passed to every agent's BT tick (manager.py:239). (2) Per-agent write: behavior/agent_behaviors.py:454 chooses a per-agent random rest location ('central_park' or 'downtown_cafe') and lines 460-463 write it into the shared dict under the single key 'take_a_short_rest'; a second agent's PlanPathToRestLocation overwrites the first agent's entry, and since neither 'take_a_short_rest' nor 'eat_at_cafe' exists in config.py's ACTIVITY_DATA (grep confirms), the config dict is permanently mutated. (3) Corruption read: agent_behaviors.py:81 (IsAtActivityLocation) reads world_state['activity_data'][agent.current_activity]['location'], so agent A with current_activity 'take_a_short_rest' would be validated against agent B's last-written location, exactly as described (navigation itself uses per-agent agent.rest_location at lines 456-458, so only the validation/cost lookups read the clobbered entry). (4) PlanPathToEatLocation does the identical write at lines 510-513 with a constant location — harmless today, as the finding states. findings.title: ShouldSocialize always fails for agents who are neither 'extrovert' nor 'introvert' — Diana can never voluntarily socialize
findings.description: ShouldSocialize.tick (lines 114-126) only returns SUCCESS inside two personality-gated branches: 'extrovert' in personality_names (line 119) or 'introvert' in personality_names (line 123). Diana's personality is ['agreeable', 'conscientious', 'fitness_enthusiast'] (config.py:325), matching neither, so the node returns FAILURE unconditionally for her regardless of her numeric social need (which still rises via entities.py:86) — her free-time socialize branch is dead. Currently latent because the free-time branch is itself unreachable (F07), but it becomes a per-agent dead branch the moment that is fixed. Even matching agents rarely pass: extroverts need random() < 0.32 and introverts < 0.09 per tick.
findings.fix: Add a default case driven by the numeric social need/talkativeness/social_motivation traits (e.g. socialize when social_need > 50 with moderate probability) rather than trait-name string matching.

Her social need still rises at simulation/entities.py:85-86 (default social_motivation 1.0, since agreeable/conscientious/fitness_enthusiast define no social_motivation per config.py:16,17,20). The probability figures are correct: extrovert talkativeness 0.8 (config.py:14) gives 0.32/tick; introvert 0.3 (config.py:15) gives 0.09/tick. findings.title: Blocked-path replanning omits `agent_<id>` destinations: agents walking to talk to someone get stuck, spamming logs and memories every tick
findings.description: Initial path planning handles three destination forms: agent_<id> (manager.py:250-255), '*home*' (256-258), and named places (259-265). The blocked-path replanning block (manager.py:291-303) only handles '*home*' and named places — for destination_name='agent_bella', world_state['places'].get('agent_bella') returns None, target_pos stays None, and neither the path nor the state changes. The agent stays 'moving' with the same blocked next_pos, so every subsequent tick re-enters the block at manager.py:288-289 and appends 'My path to agent_bella is blocked...' to its log AND its unbounded memory stream (entities.py:62-69) until the blocking agent happens to move; two agents approaching each other can block each other indefinitely (walking-toward-each-other livelock). Related gap: _find_adjacent_spot (manager.py:128-136) checks only claimed/occupied cells, not map bounds or 'G' walls, so the chosen adjacent target can be grass — BFS then fails (target fails the wall check at manager.py:20-21) and the social trip is silently aborted.
findings.fix: Add an agent_<id> branch to the replanning block (re-resolve the target agent's current position via _find_adjacent_spot), add a give-up counter that aborts on repeated failure (state='idle', clear path/interacting_with, reset the BT), and make _find_adjacent_spot verify bounds and world_layout[y][x] != 'G'.

(3) On the next tick line 245 is False (path intact, path_index < len), so the full planner never re-runs; line 285 yields the same blocked next_pos, line 288-289 re-logs "My path to agent_bella is blocked" every tick; _update_agent_schedules skips 'moving' agents (92-93) and the BT ticks only when idle (238-239), so escape requires the blocker to move. (4) entities.py:62-69 caps the log at 50 but appends to memory_stream on every add_log; AgentMemoryStream.add_memory appends unbounded (memory.py:33-34), reset_daily_memories is never called anywhere, and reset_agent_diaries is a pass no-op (narrative_system.py:72-75) — memories also feed the LLM diary prompt (narrative_system.py:24,32). Sole inaccuracy: that abort is not "silent" — line 274 logs "I can't find a path to {location_name}" — a trivial wording issue in a secondary sentence that does not change mechanism or severity.
